exercises.name: Day 1: Getting Started
exercises.summary: The official first day walkthrough. Watch this once before anything else.
steps: Sit on the floor or a mat with your legs out in front of you.
Place one foot fully into the foot hammock so your heel sits deep in the pocket.
Hold a cork handle in each hand with a relaxed grip.
Sit tall, then gently pull the handles toward you until you feel a light stretch in the back of your leg.
Hold 15 to 30 seconds while breathing slowly. Never pull into pain.
Release slowly, then switch feet.
exercises.tips: The stretch should feel like a gentle 5 or 6 out of 10, never sharp. Warm up with a short walk first.

exercises.name: Correct Form Basics
exercises.summary: How to hold the device and position your body so every stretch works properly.
steps: Keep your back tall and long instead of rounding your spine to reach further.
Let the device do the reaching: the handles bring the stretch to you.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and down, away from your ears.
Move into each stretch slowly, with no bouncing or jerking.
Breathe out as you ease deeper into the stretch.
exercises.tips: If you catch yourself holding your breath, back off a little. Smooth breathing means the intensity is right.

exercises.name: The 3 Most Common Mistakes
exercises.summary: The three errors most new owners make, and how to avoid them from day one.
steps: Watch the video once all the way through.
Check your own setup against each mistake shown.
Fix one thing at a time on your next session.
exercises.tips: Worth rewatching after your first week, once you have some reps in.

exercises.name: Adjusting Stretch Intensity
exercises.summary: How to make any stretch gentler or deeper by changing your grip and posture.
steps: Grip the handles closer to the frame for a gentler stretch.
Walk your hands further down the handles to deepen the stretch.
Lean back slightly to reduce intensity, sit taller to increase it.
Change intensity only between holds, not in the middle of one.
exercises.tips: On stiff mornings start one notch gentler than you think you need.

exercises.name: Luxury Edition Features Tour
exercises.summary: Every feature of your exact model explained: foot hammock, cork handles, and the removable 2 lb FlexxBar.
steps: Watch the tour once with your device in front of you.
Find the foot hammock, cork handles, and the magnetic FlexxBar on your own unit.
Practice removing and reattaching the FlexxBar.
exercises.tips: The FlexxBar adds light resistance for strengthening moves later on. You will not need it for basic stretching.

exercises.name: Shoulder Stretch
exercises.summary: The classic CastleFlexx shoulder opener for tight desk shoulders.
steps: Stand tall and hold the device horizontally in front of you, one handle in each hand.
With arms straight, slowly raise the device up and over your head.
Go only as far behind your head as feels comfortable, then pause.
Hold 15 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Bring it back over the top just as slowly. Repeat 2 to 3 times.
exercises.tips: A wider grip makes this easier. Narrow the grip over the weeks as your shoulders open up.

exercises.name: Shoulder and Upper Body Flexibility
exercises.summary: A quick 90 second instructional covering the main upper body positions.
steps: Follow the video positions in order, holding each about 15 to 30 seconds.
Keep your ribs down and core lightly braced so the stretch stays in the shoulders and chest.
Repeat the sequence twice if you have time.
exercises.tips: Great as a mid workday reset. It takes under five minutes total.

exercises.name: Shoulder Impingement Relief
exercises.summary: A gentle position aimed at pinchy, impinged shoulders.
steps: Hold one handle and let the frame hang behind your back.
Reach your other hand behind your lower back and take the far handle or frame.
Gently pull down with the lower hand to ease the top shoulder into a stretch.
Hold 15 to 20 seconds, then swap sides.
exercises.tips: Impingement pain that is sharp or gets worse is a sign to stop and see a professional. This should feel like relief, not aggravation.

exercises.name: Top 3 Upper Body Stretches
exercises.summary: The three upper body moves CastleFlexx recommends most, in one short video.
steps: Do the three stretches in the order shown.
Hold each for 15 to 30 seconds per side.
Keep a tall posture and relaxed neck throughout.
exercises.tips: Pairs well with the Lat and Forearm Stretch for a complete upper body session.

exercises.name: Three Upper Body Stretches (alternate set)
exercises.summary: A second short set of upper body moves for variety.
steps: Follow the video, holding each position 15 to 30 seconds.
Alternate this set with the Top 3 set on different days.
exercises.tips: Variety keeps you consistent. Rotate the two upper body sets so it never gets stale.

exercises.name: Lat and Forearm Stretch
exercises.summary: Opens the big muscles down the side of your back plus the forearms, both punished by mouse and keyboard work.
steps: Anchor one end of the device and take a handle with one hand.
Sit or kneel, then lean your body away from the anchored side until you feel the stretch along your side and lat.
Hold 15 to 30 seconds, breathing into your ribs.
For the forearm portion, follow the wrist position shown in the video.
Swap sides.
exercises.tips: If you feel it mostly in the shoulder joint rather than the side of your back, reduce the lean and reset your posture.

exercises.name: Neutral Spine, Seated
exercises.summary: How to find a neutral, stacked spine while sitting. The foundation for fixing desk posture and neck strain.
steps: Sit on the front half of your chair, feet flat on the floor.
Rock your pelvis forward and back a few times, then settle in the middle.
Stack your ribs over your pelvis and let your head float up tall.
Tuck your chin slightly so your ears line up over your shoulders.
Hold for 5 slow breaths. Repeat several times through your workday.
exercises.tips: This is the single best habit for computer related neck pain. Set a reminder to do it every hour.

exercises.name: Neutral Spine, Lying Down
exercises.summary: Learn what a relaxed neutral back feels like while lying down, so you can find it anywhere.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Gently flatten your lower back to the floor, then arch it slightly, a few times.
Settle in the comfortable middle position between the two.
Breathe slowly for one to two minutes, letting the back muscles let go.
exercises.tips: Nice way to end the day or decompress after a long sitting session.

exercises.name: The Back Pain Fix Explained
exercises.summary: Why tight hamstrings and hips so often cause lower back pain, and how the device addresses it.
steps: Watch the short explanation.
Then pair it with the hamstring and hip stretches in this tool. That combination is the actual treatment.
exercises.tips: Most desk related lower back pain improves when the hamstrings and hip flexors loosen. Work those two groups consistently.

exercises.name: Stretching While Sitting in a Chair
exercises.summary: A full routine you can do at your desk without getting on the floor. Ideal for work breaks.
steps: Sit tall near the edge of your chair.
Place one heel in the foot hammock and extend that leg forward.
Hold the handles and gently pull to stretch the back of the leg. Hold 15 to 30 seconds.
Follow the video through the remaining seated positions for the back and neck.
Switch legs and repeat.
exercises.tips: Keep the device next to your desk. A two minute version of this beats a perfect session you never do.

exercises.name: Quick Seated Stretch
exercises.summary: The fastest version of the seated hamstring stretch. Under a minute.
steps: Sit on the floor with both legs extended.
Put one foot in the foot hammock, holding a handle in each hand.
Sit tall, then hinge slightly forward from the hips while pulling gently.
Hold 20 to 30 seconds, then switch legs.
exercises.tips: Hinge from the hips, do not round your back to get lower. Height is not the goal, the feeling in the hamstring is.

exercises.name: Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.summary: Targets the muscles at the front of the hip that shorten from all day sitting.
steps: Kneel on one knee in a lunge position, back knee on a cushion.
Place the back foot into the foot hammock and hold the handles over your shoulder.
Keeping your torso tall, gently push your hips forward.
Add a gentle pull on the handles to deepen the stretch at the front of the back hip.
Hold 30 seconds up to 2 minutes, breathing slowly. Switch sides.
exercises.tips: Squeeze the glute of the back leg lightly. It protects your lower back and doubles the stretch quality.

exercises.name: Tight Hips GONE Routine
exercises.summary: A short guided routine that works around the whole hip: front, side, and deep glute.
steps: Follow the video positions in order.
Hold each position 20 to 30 seconds per side.
Move slowly between positions, no rushing.
exercises.tips: If you only have three minutes today, this is the one to do for sitting related stiffness.

exercises.name: Adductor and TFL Stretch
exercises.summary: Inner thigh and outer hip in one move. These two areas control how your knees track.
steps: Lie on your back with one foot in the foot hammock.
With the leg straight up, slowly let it fall out to the side, guiding with the handles.
Stop at a comfortable stretch along the inner thigh. Hold 15 to 30 seconds.
Bring the leg back up, then let it cross gently over your body for the outer hip. Hold again.
Switch legs.
exercises.tips: Keep your opposite shoulder on the floor when crossing over, the stretch stays honest that way.

exercises.name: The Dinner Plate (Groin and IT Band)
exercises.summary: CastleFlexx's signature circular sweep that covers the groin and the IT band in one smooth motion.
steps: Lie on your back with one foot in the foot hammock, leg pointing up.
Holding the handles, sweep the leg slowly in a wide circle, like tracing the rim of a dinner plate.
Pause anywhere you find a tight spot and hold for a few breaths.
Do 3 slow circles each direction, then switch legs.
exercises.tips: Slower is better. The pause on tight spots is where the improvement happens.

exercises.name: 3 Minute Flow: Glutes, Hamstrings, Groin, Hips
exercises.summary: A follow along mini session covering the whole lower posterior chain.
steps: Set up lying on a mat with the device ready.
Press play and follow along in real time.
Match the breathing cues and hold times in the video.
exercises.tips: Perfect after a workday, before dinner. Short enough that there is no excuse.

exercises.name: 5 Minute Flow: Legs and Glutes
exercises.summary: The most popular follow along on the channel. A complete lower body reset in five minutes.
steps: Get on a mat with the device and press play.
Follow each position, switching legs when cued.
Finish with the slow breathing at the end rather than skipping it.
exercises.tips: Doing this three times a week is a realistic, effective baseline for desk workers.

exercises.name: Leg Tightness Release: 5 Minute Advanced Flow
exercises.summary: A deeper follow along for when the basic holds start feeling easy.
steps: Warm up first with two minutes of easy movement.
Press play and follow along.
Back off any position that feels sharp. Advanced means deeper, not painful.
exercises.tips: Graduate to this after two or three weeks of the regular five minute flow.

exercises.name: Unlock Lower Body Tightness: 14 Minute Follow Along
exercises.summary: The full session. Everything below the waist, guided start to finish.
steps: Set aside 15 minutes, mat down, phone away.
Press play and follow along at the video's pace.
Use the gentler grip options any time a position is too intense.
exercises.tips: A great weekend session. Use the shorter flows on busy weekdays.

exercises.name: Isometric Strengthening: Posterior Chain
exercises.summary: Gentle push and hold work that builds strength in the newly gained range, so flexibility sticks.
steps: Set up in the seated hamstring position, foot in the hammock.
Instead of only pulling, gently push your leg down against the hammock while holding the handles steady.
Push at about 30 percent effort for 5 to 10 seconds, then relax and pull slightly deeper.
Repeat the push and relax cycle 3 times per leg.
exercises.tips: This push then relax trick is the fastest known way to gain range. Use it on any stretch once you know the basic version.

exercises.name: Quad Stretch: Lying vs Standing
exercises.summary: Two versions of the front of thigh stretch, so you can pick floor or standing.
steps: Lying version: lie on your side, place the top foot in the hammock behind you, and gently pull the handles over your shoulder until the front of the thigh stretches.
Standing version: stand tall holding a wall, foot in the hammock behind you, and pull gently upward.
Keep your knees close together and hips pushed slightly forward in both versions.
Hold 20 to 30 seconds per leg.
exercises.tips: If your knee complains, loosen the pull and move the stretch higher into the thigh by pushing the hips forward instead.

exercises.name: The Best Fix for Plantar Fasciitis
exercises.summary: The main foot and heel routine: calf plus arch, done seated.
steps: Sit with legs extended and place one heel deep into the foot hammock.
Gently pull the handles so your toes come toward you. You should feel the calf and the sole of the foot.
Hold 15 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Do 10 gentle pull and release repetitions to finish.
Switch feet.
exercises.tips: Feet respond to frequency. Doing this daily, even briefly, beats one long weekly session.

exercises.name: How I Fixed My Plantar Fasciitis
exercises.summary: The founder's own foot recovery routine, shown on the device.
steps: Watch the positions shown, then repeat them: heel in hammock, gentle toe pull, hold 15 to 30 seconds.
Add the slow ankle circles shown in the video.
Repeat on both feet, morning and evening if your feet are sore.
exercises.tips: Morning heel pain usually eases fastest when you stretch before your first steps of the day.

exercises.name: Plantar Fasciitis Quick Hit
exercises.summary: A fifteen second reminder of the single most useful foot position.
steps: Heel deep in the hammock, gentle pull, 20 second hold per foot.
That is the whole move. Do it whenever your feet feel tight.
exercises.tips: Bookmark this one mentally. It is the fastest useful thing you can do with the device.

exercises.name: Forearm Stretch
exercises.summary: Relief for mouse and keyboard forearms.
steps: Hold the frame vertically in front of you with one hand, palm facing away as shown in the video.
Use your other hand to gently add pressure until the forearm stretches.
Hold 15 to 30 seconds, then flip your palm the other way and repeat.
Switch arms.
exercises.tips: Do both palm directions. Computer strain usually lives on the top of the forearm, the direction people skip.

exercises.name: Tricep and Arm Strengthening
exercises.summary: Light arm strengthening using the device, originally designed for older adults, gentle for anyone.
steps: Stand tall holding the device behind your head, one hand on each handle.
Keeping elbows pointed forward and neck straight, press upward until arms are extended.
Squeeze the back of the arms at the top, then lower slowly.
Do 8 to 12 slow repetitions.
exercises.tips: Attach the 2 lb FlexxBar for a little extra resistance once bodyweight feels easy.

exercises.name: Advanced Abs
exercises.summary: A short core move using the device for resistance.
steps: Follow the position in the video, moving slowly.
Exhale on the effort, keep your lower back from arching.
Start with 2 sets of 8 and build up.
exercises.tips: A strong core takes pressure off the lower back during long sitting days.

routines.description: The desk break reset: one move each for shoulders, hamstrings and lower back, and feet.

routines.label: 10 minutes
routines.description: A guided lower body flow plus the top upper body moves. The best value for a busy day.

routines.label: 15 minutes
routines.description: Hips, glutes and hamstrings, quads, upper body, and forearms. Full desk recovery circuit.

routines.description: The full session: the 14 minute lower body follow along, then a complete upper body and feet finish.
